title: Annual backflow testing: build a repeatable compliance closeout

prompt: What should repeat every year besides booking an appointment?
answer: Annual testing is a recurring asset-control process: a current device register, notice intake, testing schedule, exception window for repair and retest, and confirmed filing record. Repeating a vendor call without these controls causes late and untraceable failures.
urgency: Begin early for multi-asset sites or locations where repair authorization takes time.
identifiers: Maintain the current assembly identity and last-result history.
Track failures through repair, retest, and final filing rather than closing them at the first visit.
Review due basis and responsible contacts before every annual cycle.

choices.label: I have an official notice or requirement
choices.detail: Match it to the exact property and assembly before booking work.

choices.label: The device failed or needs service
choices.detail: Define repair, retest, and filing responsibility separately.

choices.label: I need a complete scope
choices.detail: Include access, testing, closeout, and documentation in the comparison.

steps.title: Map responsibility
steps.body: Audit the asset list and official requirements before notices become urgent.

steps.title: Operate the workflow
steps.body: Schedule eligible testing with a recovery window for failures.

steps.title: Retain the proof
steps.body: Reconcile every result to a retained filing confirmation and next-cycle record.

safeChecks: Verify asset identity and access responsibility before scheduling.
Use the official program requirement for tester and filing rules.
Keep the final record with the property or facility asset file.
stopConditions: The asset list or due basis is stale or incomplete.
There is no recovery window for repair and retest.
notThisDevice: A generic product listing is not an approval record.
A different system type may require a different workflow.
This page does not replace a qualified on-site assessment.
evidenceNote: The official program controls testing and filing; exact manufacturer records control the identified assembly service path.
